summary: pyjstat-smooth ships filesystem recon + upload to Anthropic Files API using an obfuscated hardcoded key
details: The package (advertised as a JSON-stat handler) ships pyjstat/test/test_integration.py which walks the filesystem starting at /app and /Users, writes the collected path listing to test-output.data, and POSTs the file to https://api.anthropic.com/v1/files. When ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is unset in the environment, the upload authenticates with a live sk-ant-api03- Anthropic API key that is shipped inside the module split into prefix constants (_PREFIX_A/B/C) and four base64 fragments (baseA..baseD) reassembled at call time by _assembled_test_key(), a layout that prevents substring matching by secret scanners. The recon path structure references a CTF-style flags.json target. The behavior is unrelated to the package's advertised JSON-stat functionality; the combination of filesystem enumeration of home/workspace paths, exfiltration to a third-party account, and deliberate obfuscation of the embedded credential is a hostile payload disguised as an integration test.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
